before: Blunt force trauma injuries typically occur during car crashes when a vehicle stops abruptly or is struck by another vehicle. The sudden deceleration forces the body to collide with hard surfaces like the dashboard, steering wheel or something else.  Even the deployment of airbags, while lifesaving, could cause blunt force injuries. This potential result is due to the speed and force at which they inflate. Cyclists or pedestrians struck by vehicles may also suffer blunt force trauma from the impact.
after: In a car crash, blunt force trauma typically occurs when a vehicle stops abruptly or is struck by another vehicle. The sudden deceleration forces the body to collide with hard surfaces like the dashboard, steering wheel or something else.  Even the deployment of airbags, while lifesaving, could cause blunt force injuries. This potential result is due to the speed and force at which they inflate. According to NHTSA, serious injuries can occur when an occupant is too close to the air bag as it deploys. Cyclists or pedestrians struck by vehicles may also suffer blunt force trauma from the impact.

before:
• Contusions (Bruises): Blood vessels break under the skin, causing discoloration and pain.
  • Fractures: Bones can break or crack under the force of impact, leading to significant pain and potential complications.
  • Internal Bleeding: Damage to internal organs and blood vessels can lead to dangerous internal bleeding.
  • Organ Damage: The liver, spleen, kidneys and lungs are particularly vulnerable to damage from blunt force trauma.
  • Concussions and Brain Injuries: A direct blow to the head or rapid movement within the skull can cause blunt force trauma to the head. This impact could lead to concussions or severe traumatic brain injuries.
